issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a SealSaloon constructor that accepts a String parameter (SealSaloon(String)) for the saloon name, but both the provided template usage (Main) and the reference solution implement and expect a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()). This mismatch will confuse students about which constructor signature to implement and may cause compile errors or test failures depending on which artifact they follow.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signature consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement/UML to specify a no-argument constructor, or (B) change the template Main and the solution SealSaloon to use a constructor that accepts a String (public SealSaloon(String name)) and initialize fields accordingly (also update any calls to new SealSaloon() to pass a name). Prefer option B if the saloon name is important to the exercise.

issues.description: Problem statement specifies a SealSaloon constructor that accepts a String parameter (SealSaloon(String)) for identification, but both the provided template usage (Main) and the solution implement/use a no-argument constructor (new SealSaloon()). This signature mismatch (constructor with String vs. no-arg constructor) creates confusion for students about the required constructor signature and where to supply the saloon name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signature consistent across artifacts. Either update the solution and template to provide a constructor matching the problem (public SealSaloon(String name) { ... }) and adjust instantiations in Main to pass a name, or update the problem statement to require a no-argument constructor. Preferred fix: implement public SealSaloon(String name) in SealSaloon and update Main instantiations accordingly so the code matches the documented API.
